question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. If $v$ is an eigenvector of an invertible matrix $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =\frac{1}{3}$ then $v$ is also an eigenvector of the matrix ${A}^{-1}$ that corresponds to $\lambda =4.$

II. An eigenvector of an invertible matrix $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-2$ is also an eigenvector of the inverse ${A}^{-1}$ that corresponds to $\lambda =-\frac{1}{2}.$

III. If $v$ is an eigenvector of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$ then $5v$ is also an eigenvector of $A$ corresponding to $\lambda =15.$
